memory_candidates.content: When bulk-rewriting Lean comment text with `sed -i -E` using multiple `-e` expressions, one pattern whose replacement text contains a literal `/` (e.g. "neg/imp") silently fails the entire multi-expression parse (reports one 'unknown option to s' error) and applies NONE of the expressions, leaving the file unchanged with no partial progress. The fix is to either pick a different `sed` delimiter for that one expression, or switch to a Python string-replace (`str.replace`) for the whole batch when any pattern contains a literal `/`. Always re-grep after a multi-`-e` sed to confirm it actually applied before moving on.

When clearing a repo-wide text-pattern lint (e.g. task-number citations) across a large file set, re-deriving the scoped occurrence count per subtree BEFORE editing and comparing it against the plan's pre-computed scope hypothesis is a cheap, high-value correctness check: an exact match confirms no drift happened between plan-authoring and implementation time, while a mismatch surfaces scope-hypothesis staleness immediately rather than silently under- or over-fixing.
